answer: Give every agent a quill, not a megaphone: identity is a writing instrument, and sybil resistance is the difference between authorship and repetition. Each graded epoch is a terrace of published work — original text, countersigned, hash-chained to the last — and a beacon lights only on the highest terrace where the work stands uncontradicted. Copyists can replumb megaphones all night; a copied page is not a written one, and the beacon never lights on plagiarism. Payouts and seats read terraces, so depth of authored work is the only climb that pays.
